content.synthesis:
Identity, funding trajectory, and group capacity form a coherent picture for this lead. Allison N. Jaynes is the University of Iowa's tenured (effective 2022) Associate Professor running the **Magnetospheric & Auroral Dynamics Lab (MAD Lab)** with a research footprint spanning auroral precipitation - magnetosphere coupling (SWORD $476K), radiation-belt physics (NSF 2452400 PI $51K active 2025-2028), auroral sounding-rocket instrumentation (TRA-SR/COUSIN/LAMPSat), and graduate-fellowship-driven student sponsorship (FINESST 2026). Compared to her CV-only awards from the early 2020s (CAREER 2021-2025, HTIDeS 2021-2024), her 2024-2026 portfolio tilts heavier toward **multi-institutional collaborations** (SWORD with CU Boulder, GEM collaborative NSF, SSMSD TRACERS equipment) than solo PI grants - a common mid-career pattern where a PI moves from start-up-style single-PI awards to leading portions of larger center-style efforts. The FINESST 2026 award shows the deliberate ramp of graduate-student first-authorship funding inside the group, with Daneshmand as the named fellow - a recurring pattern (Riley Troyer 2023 PhD advised by Jaynes per the CV) of advisors trading postdoc authorship for student-driven fellowships as the group matures.

Capacity diagnostic: with three named postdocs (Hill, Joseph, Feltman) and four named PhD students (McLennan, Daneshmand, Powers, Minot) on the public People page, the group has no public opening, matching the absence of a posted vacancy. This is the standard signal that a group is at saturation - pushing outreach toward "soft" inbound interest ("are you taking rotations?") rather than "apply now" CTA. Jessberger-type hypothesis: if the LinkedIn `jobs count: 1` resolves to a hidden posting, expect it to be either a research-associate position supporting SWORD instrumentation (akin to the SSMSD equipment line) or a postdoctoral position extending the SWORD or NSF 2452400 workstream; both would be consistent with the post-2024 funding direction.

Risk-flag: the SWORD announcement tied UIowa to a CU Boulder-led center via Tom Berger; any UIowa continuation beyond the SWORD-funded postdoc (Shannon Hill) would require either the CU Boulder center continuing or a UIowa-led center grant succeeding - so the lead's funding outlook past 2027 hinges on her next NSF or NASA ROSES center-line submission. None of that is a "funds available for a PhD" claim - it is interpretive context.
